title: fix(app-shell): retire the unreachable flow node-type shim; keep the sharing_rule opt-out on its real, re-measured reason
body:
Fixes #6982

Both named cures in `clientValidation.ts` were re-measured against the spec this repo actually resolves (`@objectstack/spec` **17.2.0**, pin `^17.0.0`). The card's own `safeParse` readings were run by its filer, and the triage seat explicitly declined to re-run them — so everything below is measured again from scratch on this branch. **Both of the card's readings reproduce.** The two halves then reach *opposite* verdicts, which is the substance of this PR.

| half | card's reading | reproduces? | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 — flow node-type shim | unreachable dead code | ✅ yes | **removed** |
| 2 — `sharing_rule` opt-out | stated reason has expired | ✅ yes | **opt-out KEPT** — the reason moved, the boundary did not |

---

## Half 1 — `FORWARD_COMPAT_FLOW_NODE_TYPES` was unreachable. Removed.

The shim suppressed one thing: an issue addressed to `nodes.N.type` whose node's own `type` was `approval` or `connector_action`, back when the published `FlowNodeSchema.type` was a closed enum. ADR-0019 P2 opened that field and has since reached npm.

```
FlowSchema.safeParse({name,label,type:'autolaunched',nodes:[{id,type:T,label}],edges:[]})
  T = 'approval'              ACCEPT
  T = 'connector_action'      ACCEPT
  T = 'zzz_made_up_node_type' ACCEPT      <- open string, not a widened enum
  T = ''                      REJECT  nodes.0.type / too_small
```

Unreachable, not merely redundant. I swept 7 malformed-node variants across both shim node types — 14 probes — asking whether *any* of them can put an issue on `nodes.N.type` while that node's type is one the shim names:

```
SHIM COULD FIRE IN: 0 of 14 probes
```

Every rejection lands elsewhere (`nodes.0.label`, `nodes.0.id`, `nodes.0/unrecognized_keys`, `nodes.0.config`). The only issue that path still yields is `too_small` on the empty string — and the shim **already kept** that one, because `nodeTypeAt` returned the falsy `''`. Same for a non-string type, where it returned `undefined`. So the deletion moves no verdict in any direction.

Removed: the shim set, its `FLOW_NODE_TYPE_ISSUE` regex, `nodeTypeAt`, and the `if (type === 'flow')` filter block. All four were module-local. The two prose mentions (`validateMetadataDraft`'s JSDoc, `ResourceEditPage`'s skew paragraph) now record the retirement instead of pointing at a deleted symbol.

New pin `clientValidation.flowNodeTypes.test.ts` makes the deletion falsifiable: if a future spec re-closes that enum — the exact condition the shim existed for — it goes red and names the premise that came back. The arbitrary-node-type case is deliberate; one accepted literal cannot distinguish "the enum opened" from "the enum listed two more literals".

---

## Half 2 — ⛔ the opt-out STAYS. The gate would refuse bodies the server accepts.

The card is **right** that the stated reason expired. Re-measured on 17.2.0:

```
SharingRuleSchema declared keys: name, label, description, object, active,
  accessLevel, sharedWith, _lock, _lockReason, _lockSource, _provenance,
  _packageId, _packageVersion, _lockDocsUrl, type, condition
envelope keys declared: 7/7    MISSING: none
```

The contract-first repair landed. But removing the opt-out on the strength of that is the trap, because **a served body carries more than the envelope.**

The read path decorates every served item with `_diagnostics`, and the spec deliberately does *not* allowlist it the way it allowlists the envelope — `kernel/metadata-read-decorations.ts` says a served body "is therefore NOT a valid input to the schema that produced it until these are removed". `SharingRuleSchema` is still `.strict()`.

**Measured on the real read path** — the objectstack protocol over a real engine, save then read back, not schema-shape reasoning:

```
GET .../sharing_rule/west_accounts             item keys += _diagnostics  -> REJECT
GET .../sharing_rule/west_accounts?state=draft item keys += _diagnostics  -> REJECT
layered `effective` (RAW, undecorated)                                    -> ACCEPT

ResourceEditPage edit-door draft = {...layered.effective, ...getDraft().item}
  >>> EDIT-DOOR GATE VERDICT: REJECT  (root)/unrecognized_keys keys=["_diagnostics"]
```

`ResourceEditPage` assembles the edit draft exactly that way and strips nothing, so **any sharing rule with a pending draft** would reach a switched-on gate carrying `_diagnostics`. The server, by contrast, strips read decorations on the way in and never re-parses stored rows through this registry at all — the body PUTs back byte-identical.

The `serverSchema.required` root-cure cannot take this back out: it only suppresses **absent** top-level fields (`path.length === 1`), and `unrecognized_keys` arrives at the **root**.

That is the objectstack#5316 inversion wearing a different key, and the same class the framework has already paid for twice: a served `_diagnostics` 400ing every saved dataset, and the cold-boot flow bind (cloud#971). Per the dispatch brief, a gate that refuses legitimate author input is worse than the defense-in-depth gap it closes, so **nothing on the security surface was loosened and the gate was not switched on.** `AUTHOR_SHAPE_ONLY_TYPES` still reads `new Set(['sharing_rule'])`, byte-identical.

What *did* change is the drift the card filed: the block's stated reason is now the measured one, so the next reader does not re-derive "the envelope landed, therefore delete this".

### The old pin had gone toothless

`clientValidation.optOuts.test.ts` guarded this boundary with a `_packageId`-stamped body. On 17.2.0 that key is declared, so the schema accepts it on **both** doors — the pin could no longer tell "opt-out in place" from "opt-out deleted". Replaced with a `_diagnostics` pin that bites, plus a counter-measurement on the create door so a schema that quietly stopped being strict cannot leave it green.

### Reverse verification — predicted before running

Prediction: emptying the set turns the new `_diagnostics` pin **red** and leaves the envelope pin **green**.

| assertion | measured |
|:--|:--|
| `does not gate the edit door — a served body carries _diagnostics` | 🔴 `unrecognized_keys: _diagnostics` |
| `reports the edit door as having NO client validator` | 🔴 *(missed prediction — see below)* |
| `does not gate the edit door — a stored body may carry _packageId` | 🟢 **stayed green — the toothlessness, confirmed** |

Predicted 1 red, measured 2. The miss is honest and worth recording: the suite already had one assertion that catches the deletion (`hasClientValidator(..., 'edit')`), so it was never *fully* toothless — but that one says only *that* the door is shut, never *why*. The suite header now states this distinction rather than my original over-claim.

Ablation discipline: mutation confirmed on disk before measuring (old-text occurrences 0, injected-text 1, blob `34aff83b` ≠ HEAD blob `bd0415be`), restore leg verified by `git diff HEAD` empty and the blob back to `bd0415be`, `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with an absolute repo root throughout. No rebuild was needed: the suite imports `./clientValidation` relatively, i.e. source-direct, with no `exports`-resolved `dist` in the path.

---

## Scope, and one thing found on the way

Entirely within `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/`. Nothing lands in `packages/types` or the spec.

**Clause-②: `no`, verified from this diff** — zero `export` lines added or removed; all four symbols touched (`FORWARD_COMPAT_FLOW_NODE_TYPES`, `FLOW_NODE_TYPE_ISSUE`, `nodeTypeAt`, `AUTHOR_SHAPE_ONLY_TYPES`) were module-local at the base commit; no key declared, no published schema moved. Per the 2026-08-28 negative boundary, a runtime security **behaviour** change would not be Clause-② either — and this one does not even change behaviour.

Filed separately as **#7603**, out of scope here and left for PM triage: the `_diagnostics` ingress above is not specific to sharing rules. Every wired `.strict()` type gates both doors today, so an item **with a pending draft** already reaches its edit gate carrying `_diagnostics` — measured on `flow`: clean body ACCEPT, body plus `_diagnostics` REJECT. `sharing_rule` is accidentally the only type shielded, by this very opt-out. Advisory rather than Save-blocking, so the cost is a false "invalid" banner, not a wedge. That issue stays open on its own.

## Verification

Union re-run on the final commit `5e44d2a9`:

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/
  -> Test Files 225 passed (225)   Tests 2331 passed | 1 skipped (2332)

pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build && pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check
  -> exit 0; 0 `error TS` lines (script name echoed, so it really ran)

node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs
  -> exit 0; empty-frontmatter changeset declared as releasing nothing

pnpm lint          (full repo — NOT narrowed; 47 lint tasks, all successful)
  -> 0 errors across every package; warnings are pre-existing no-explicit-any.
     None of the four changed files produced a single finding.
```

Empty frontmatter is the honest declaration: the shim removal is measured behaviour-preserving, and the remainder is comments and tests.

Notes on how these were run, so they are reproducible: vitest from the **repo root** with a path filter (this repo's guard refuses a package-directory run, and a package-cwd run silently reports another package's 22 files as green). `type-check` is spelled with a hyphen here — the first attempt without the dependency closure built produced 100+ `TS2307 Cannot find module '@object-ui/*'`, which is the unbuilt-closure signature, not a type error in this diff. All heavy runs went through `objectstack/scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`; the wall-clock figures in its VERDICT lines are shared-box readings, not idle-machine ones.
